description:
Explorer thumbnails for 435 file types Windows can't read, plus a right-click image toolkit. SageThumbs 2K is a modern, crash-isolated Windows 11 shell extension written in Rust that rebuilds the classic SageThumbs. It gives File Explorer thumbnails for 435 file types Windows can't preview on its own — camera RAW, HEIC/AVIF, Photoshop, DjVu, ebooks and comics, video frames, 3D-print files and a long tail of obscure formats — plus a right-click image toolkit (convert, resize, rotate, OCR, color picker, metadata strip, combine-to-PDF/CBZ) and a console/AI CLI. Free for personal use.
## TL;DR **≡ƒåò New** - **iPhone and iPad app packages (.ipa) show their app icon**, the way .apk shows its launcher icon (#88) **≡ƒöü Changed** - **Settings: Data & Backup shows your sync sign-in in the Basic view too, either who you are signed in as or an offer to sign in** **≡ƒ⌐╣ Fixed** - **Android apps whose launcher icon is an adaptive vector icon show that icon instead of an unrelated picture from inside the app** (an app whose icon does not resolve keeps the stock icon, and no longer gets a random drawable). Its linear and radial gradient fills are drawn, and a fill that cannot be resolved is left empty rather than painted black - **Apple-crushed (CgBI) PNGs copied out of iOS apps get a thumbnail** - **Comics and archives copied from a Mac no longer lose their thumbnail to macOS `._` sidecar files** - **DOS-EPS files whose only preview is WMF get a thumbnail** (drawn by ImageMagick, so on the full install only) - **Quick preview: arrowing through a folder no longer gets stuck on a video; the arrows seek only once you start interacting with the clip**
Read more: everything in 5.1.0 - **iPhone and iPad app packages (.ipa) show their app icon (#88).** The icon is the one the app's `Info.plist` names (XML or binary), found in its `Payload/.app` folder: the store-size `iTunesArtwork` picture first, then the largest listed `AppIcon` PNG, then the app folder's own `AppIcon*.png`. An IPA that names no readable icon keeps the stock icon, never a picture bundled inside it. - **Settings: Data & Backup shows your sync sign-in in the Basic view too.** Signed in, the page says who you are signed in as and offers Stop syncing; signed out, it offers to sign in, in the same words as the sign-in banner. Before, the sync row lived only in the Advanced view. - **Android apps whose launcher icon is an adaptive vector icon show that icon instead of an unrelated picture from inside the app.** Some apps ship their launcher icon only as an adaptive icon (a background and a foreground layer) or a vector drawing, with no PNG icon anywhere. The .apk reader used to take some other picture from the app's resources instead. It now draws the icon from its layers, including their linear and radial gradient fills (a sweep gradient is drawn in its first colour); a fill that cannot be resolved is left empty, as Android leaves it, rather than painted black. An app whose launcher icon does not resolve at all keeps the stock icon instead of getting a random picture from its resources. - **Apple-crushed (CgBI) PNGs copied out of iOS apps get a thumbnail.** Xcode writes its app icons as CgBI PNGs (raw deflate, BGRA order, premultiplied alpha), which no stock decoder reads. The image tier now decodes them with their true colours, standalone or inside an .ipa. - **Comics and archives copied from a Mac no longer lose their thumbnail to macOS `._` sidecar files.** A Mac copying to a FAT, exFAT or SMB drive leaves an AppleDouble `._` file beside each page, and zipping or tarring on Windows keeps them. Those sidecars sorted ahead of the real page and became the cover, but their bytes are an AppleDouble header, not a picture, so the archive got no thumbnail. They are now skipped as junk, like `__MACOSX` and `Thumbs.db`. - **DOS-EPS files whose only preview is WMF get a thumbnail.** A DOS-EPS with no TIFF preview used to keep its stock icon. Its WMF preview is now the cover, drawn by the ImageMagick tier. The compact install has no ImageMagick, so it still shows the stock icon for these files. - **Quick preview: arrowing through a folder no longer gets stuck on a video.** Before, a video that autoplayed while you arrowed through photos took over ΓåÉ/ΓåÆ, which then seeked it by 5 s and kept you on that clip. Now a clip you reach by arrowing starts with ΓåÉ/ΓåÆ still moving between files; they seek only once you press a transport key (K, P, M, L, Home/End, Γåæ/Γåô) or click the transport strip. A clip you open directly still seeks with ΓåÉ/ΓåÆ as before. - **Licence page:** the plan and licence status come first, with the rest folded behind two tap-to-open rows, and signing in asks the licence server about your account at once, so a licence held by the account shows straight away instead of Free with trials.
